planting.note: Plant rooted stem cuttings after last frost against a sturdy post or trellis in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; red dragon fruit is distinguished from the more common yellow and white-fleshed types by its vivid magenta-red flesh and skin.

directions: Plant rooted cuttings against a sturdy post, arbor, or trellis in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; red dragon fruit is a climbing, epiphyte-rooting cactus that needs strong support to carry its heavy, triangular, segmented stems as they scramble upward and produce aerial roots along the way. Enormous, night-blooming, fragrant white flowers open for a single night in summer, and if hand-pollinated (many red-fleshed cultivars benefit from pollen from a second Hylocereus type for best fruit set), they develop into vivid magenta-skinned fruit with intensely colored, sweet, deep red to magenta flesh, richer flavored and more strikingly colored than the more commonly sold white or yellow-fleshed dragon fruit. Fruit typically forms about a month after successful pollination and is ready to pick once the skin color deepens and the fruit gives slightly to gentle pressure. It needs consistent warmth and is intolerant of frost, so grow it only in essentially tropical, frost-free gardens or as a large container specimen moved under cover for winter elsewhere.
sources: USDA ARS National Plant Germplasm System (GRIN-Global)
